chunks.title: RoFR & Tribal Land Advocacy
chunks.text: Securing individual (IFR) and community forest rights (CFR) for Adivasi families under the Forest Rights Act 2006, protecting over 15,000+ acres of ancestral forests. Components: IFR & CFR Claims Documentation, Gram Sabha Resolution Filing, GPS Boundary Demarcation, Title Deed (Patta) Distribution Support.

chunks.title: Community Forest Resource (CFR) Mapping
chunks.text: Gram Sabha resource committees in the Rampachodavaram and Chinturu ITDA tracts map and document community forest use, from shifting cultivation plots to bamboo and minor forest produce collection grounds. Components: Village Resource Mapping, NTFP & Bamboo Harvest Records, Sacred Grove (Punya Vanalu) Protection, CFR Claim Drafting Support.

chunks.title: Land Transfer Regulation 1 of 1970 Restitution
chunks.text: Recovery of tribal land illegally alienated to non-tribals in the K.R. Puram ITDA belt, through revenue petitions, mutation follow-up and litigation support for dispossessed families. Components: Alienation Case Survey, Revenue & Mutation Petitions, Patta Restoration Follow-Up, Victim Family Legal Aid.

chunks.title: Forest Rights Act Literacy Camps
chunks.text: Hamlet-level legal literacy sessions that explain the IFR and CFR claim process, Forest Rights Committee formation, and the evidence required before the Sub-Divisional Level Committee. Components: Bare Act Village Readings, Claim Helpdesk Assistance, Forest Rights Committee Formation, SDLC & DLC Hearing Support.

chunks.title: Self-Governance & PESA Act 1996
chunks.text: Mobilizing Adivasi hamlets to exercise sovereign powers vested in the Gram Sabha under PESA, curbing illegal land alienation and defending customary heritage. Components: Gram Sabha Capacity Training, PESA Rules Enforcement, Dispute Resolution Through Tribal Elders, Natural Resource Governance.

chunks.title: Gram Sabha Panchayat & Planning Training
chunks.text: Training elected Gram Sabha Panchayats to prepare village development plans, assert minor-water-forest and land entitlement powers, and hold statutory meetings in the mother tongue. Components: Annual Village Planning, PESA Powers Orientation, Minutes & Record Keeping, Women Councillor Mentoring.

chunks.title: Elder Council Dispute Resolution
chunks.text: Customary justice forums convened by tribal elders and Gram Sabhas settle land, family and resource disputes locally, reducing case pendency and court costs for Adivasi families. Components: Elder Council Convening, Customary Law Documentation, Land Dispute Mediation, Referral To Legal Aid Cell.

chunks.title: RTI & Departmental Convergence Monitoring
chunks.text: Using the Right to Information Act and ITDA review meetings to track sanctioned works, welfare scheme entitlements and service delivery in agency mandals. Components: RTI Representations, ITDA Convergence Reviews, Scheme Utilisation Audits, Grievance Escalation Tracking.

chunks.title: Land Acquisition (LA) & R&R Advocacy
chunks.text: Defending rights of 1,05,000+ Project Displaced Families (PDFs) facing displacement from the Polavaram National Project under the RFCTLARR Act 2013. Components: Fair Market Land Valuation, Adult Youth (18+) Package Claims, Colony Amenities Monitoring, High Court Litigation Support.

chunks.id: program:R&R Social Audit of Submerged Villages
chunks.title: R&R Social Audit of Submerged Villages
chunks.text: Independent community social audits across the 371 submergence-area villages of the tri-ITDA belt, verifying beneficiary lists, compensation records and resettlement entitlements. Components: Household Survey Verification, Beneficiary List Audits, Village-Level Social Audit Meetings, Audit Findings Submissions.

chunks.title: RFCTLARR Act 2013 Entitlement Tracking
chunks.text: Section-by-section tracking of land-for-land and house-for-house entitlements, homestead plots, amenities and rehabilitation grants for project-affected families. Components: Entitlement Register Maintenance, Land-for-Land Verification, Housing Plot Allocation Review, Resettlement Colony Amenities.

chunks.title: PAF Grievance Redressal & Litigation Support
chunks.text: Grievance camps and court support for project-affected families whose awards, pensions and colony works remain unresolved, including documentation for writ petitions. Components: PAF Grievance Camps, Award Objection Filing, Rehabilitation Commissioner Representations, Writ Petition Documentation.

chunks.title: Antyodaya: Matsya Mithra Women Federation
chunks.text: Empowering 3,500+ Yenadi tribal fisherwomen across 6 coastal mandals of Krishna District through sustainable fisheries, cold storage, and micro-credit. Components: Fisheries Cooperatives Management, Micro-Savings & SHG Linkages, Direct Market Fish Processing, Leadership & Gender Justice.

chunks.title: Yenadi House-Site Pattas & Identity Documents
chunks.text: Securing permanent house-site pattas and civil documentation for nomadic Yenadi hamlets in Machilipatnam, Bantumilli and Koduru mandals so families can claim ration, pension and school access. Components: House-Site Patta Filing, Aadhaar & Voter Enrolment, Ration Card Linking, Pension Scheme Access.

chunks.title: Micro-Savings & Revolving Credit Groups
chunks.text: Savings collectives run by Matsya Mithra members replace moneylender debt with internal revolving loans, steady repayments and financial literacy for coastal households. Components: Weekly Savings Meetings, Revolving Loan Corpus, Debt-Free Livelihood Support, Book-Keeping Training.

chunks.title: Estuarine Fishing Rights & Mangrove Care
chunks.text: Women-led committees in the Kruthivennu and Nagayalanka creeks protect artisanal fishing zones, ban destructive fine-mesh trawling and restore mangrove tidal barriers. Components: Artisanal Zone Protection, Mangrove Regeneration Drives, Breeding Season Norms, Cyclone Shelter Preparedness.

chunks.title: Child Interventions & Bare Acts
chunks.text: Ensuring every Adivasi child enjoys statutory protection under RTE, Juvenile Justice, and POCSO Acts, supporting bilingual education and nutrition. Components: Anti-Child Labor & Trafficking Vigilance, Mother-Tongue Bilingual Learning, Malnutrition Mitigation in Ashram Schools, Child Bare Acts Community Workshops.

chunks.id: program:Joyful Learning Centres in Agency Hamlets
chunks.title: Joyful Learning Centres in Agency Hamlets
chunks.text: Village learning centres that teach young children in Koya and Telugu mother tongues, with tribal folk content, play-based material and no corporal punishment. Components: Mother-Tongue Pedagogy, Folk & Cultural Curricula, Toy & Learning Material Kits, Volunteer Teacher Support.

chunks.title: Digital Classrooms & School Support Kits
chunks.text: School kits, uniforms, footwear and digital learning equipment supplied to Adivasi children in ashram and village schools to curb dropouts in the Godavari belt. Components: Uniform & Footwear Support, Digital Classroom Equipment, Exam & Career Guidance, Dropout Re-Enrolment Drives.

chunks.title: Child Protection & Nutrition Watch
chunks.text: Community vigilance on child labour, trafficking and residential-school nutrition, with reporting pathways to Child Welfare Committees and district authorities. Components: Residential School Inspections, Nutrition & Meal Monitoring, Childline & CWC Linkages, POCSO Awareness Sessions.

chunks.title: Flood Relief Measures (2020 – 2023)
chunks.text: Mobilizing emergency boat rescues, essential food provisions, sanitary supplies, and winter blankets for Godavari and Krishna river flood victims. Components: Boat Rescue & Evacuation Teams, Ration & Medical Kit Distribution, Post-Flood Sanitation & Water Purification, Housing Rehabilitation Assistance.

chunks.title: Godavari Gorge Rescue & Evacuation
chunks.text: Volunteer boat teams reach isolated riverside habitations in the Kunavaram and Devipatnam gorge belt during monsoon inundation, moving families to relief camps. Components: Community Boat Teams, Isolated Hamlet Access, Relief Camp Setup, Livestock & Grain Shift Support.

chunks.title: Winter Blanket & Health Drives
chunks.text: Blankets, warm clothing and basic medical checks for exposed hill hamlets during Eastern Ghats winter, when cold stress hits children and elders hardest. Components: Blanket Distribution, Mobile Health Checks, Elder & Child Care Kits, Village Health Referrals.

chunks.title: Post-Flood Sanitation & Safe Water
chunks.text: Disinfection, clean drinking water units and latrine restoration after Godavari and Krishna floods, plus rebuilding support for damaged houses. Components: Water Purification Units, Village Disinfection Works, Damaged House Repair, Sanitary & Dignity Kits.

chunks.title: Community Solar & Green Energy
chunks.text: Providing decentralized clean solar home lighting systems and solar street poles to remote, un-electrified hill habitations across the Eastern Ghats. Components: Solar Street Pole Installations, Portable Solar Lantern Distribution, Local Youth Technician Training, Zero-Carbon Rural Electrification.

chunks.id: program:Solar Home Lighting for Off-Grid Hamlets
chunks.title: Solar Home Lighting for Off-Grid Hamlets
chunks.text: Decentralized solar lighting systems installed in Godavari gorge hamlets cut off from the conventional grid, replacing kerosene lamps in Adivasi households. Components: Household Solar Kits, Kerosene-Free Habitats, Installation Site Survey, Beneficiary Handover Training.

chunks.title: Solar Street Poles & Water Units
chunks.text: Solar street lighting at village meeting points and schools improves night safety for women and children, alongside solar-assisted drinking water purification. Components: Village Lane Street Poles, School & Path Lighting, Solar Water Purification, Community Maintenance Corpus.

chunks.title: Tribal Youth Solar Technician Training
chunks.text: Local Adivasi youth are trained to service solar kits, replace batteries and maintain micro-grids, keeping repair work and income inside the village. Components: Panel & Battery Servicing, Fault Diagnosis Modules, Village Maintenance Teams, Green Livelihood Linkages.

chunks.title: Indigenous Millets & Seed Banks
chunks.text: Reviving native heritage millet cultivation, bio-fertilizers, and community heirloom seed banks to guarantee food sovereignty and climate resilience. Components: Traditional Millet Cultivation, Community Indigenous Seed Banks, Chemical-Free Organic Farming, Soil & Water Conservation Works.

chunks.title: Community Heirloom Seed Banks
chunks.text: Farmer-managed seed stores preserve native millet, pulse and oilseed varieties, distributed before each sowing season without cost to small and marginal growers. Components: Variety Selection & Storage, Seed Exchange Festivals, Farmer Steward Committees, Germination & Viability Tests.

chunks.title: Natural Farming & Bio-Input Fields
chunks.text: Chemical-free plot demonstrations using farmyard inputs, composting and intercropping, so degraded agency slopes regain soil health and lower input costs. Components: Bio-Fertilizer Preparation, Compost & Mulch Training, Intercropping Models, Pest Management Without Chemicals.

chunks.title: Water Conservation & Farm Ponds
chunks.text: Contour bunding, percolation tanks and farm ponds dug with Gram Sabha labour to hold monsoon runoff for dry-season millet and vegetable cultivation. Components: Farm Pond Construction, Contour & Trench Binding, Drip & Mica Irrigation Support, Kitchen Garden Promotion.

chunks.title: What is ALERT and when was it founded?
chunks.text: ALERT (Association for Land and Livelihood) was founded in 2004 (Registration No. 307/2004) under the Societies Registration Act. Headquartered in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, ALERT is dedicated to empowering Adivasis and marginalized coastal communities in the Fifth Scheduled areas through rights-based development, legal aid, and environmental sustainability.

chunks.title: What is the Forest Rights Act (RoFR) and how does ALERT assist?
chunks.text: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 recognizes the pre-existing rights of forest-dwelling tribal communities over ancestral lands and minor forest produce. ALERT assists Gram Sabhas with field mapping, gathering revenue evidence, and submitting Individual Forest Rights (IFR) and Community Forest Rights (CFR) claims.

chunks.title: How does ALERT support families displaced by the Polavaram Irrigation Project (PIP)?
chunks.text: ALERT tracks land valuation awards, coordinates legal petitions before the High Court of AP and the R&R Commissioner Office, monitors housing colony amenities (drinking water, schooling, roads), and operates a community grievance redressal cell to ensure every displaced family and adult youth receives their statutory package.

chunks.title: What is the role of PESA in tribal self-governance?
chunks.text: The Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA), 1996 vests mandatory authority in the village Gram Sabha. In Schedule V areas, no land acquisition, minor water body alienation, or mining lease can proceed without prior consultation and resolution by the Gram Sabha. ALERT trains tribal leaders and Gram Sabha members in exercising these statutory powers.

chunks.title: Are donations to ALERT eligible for income tax exemption?
chunks.text: Yes. ALERT is registered under Section 12A and Section 80G of the Indian Income Tax Act. Donors receive a formal 80G tax receipt allowing them to claim up to a 50% deduction on their taxable income as permitted under Indian tax laws.

chunks.title: How can individuals or organizations volunteer or collaborate with ALERT?
chunks.text: We welcome interns, legal researchers, environmental scientists, and volunteers. Opportunities include field research in tribal mandals, documentation of oral histories, child education initiatives, and disaster relief logistics. You can reach out through our Contact page or write directly to director@alertngo.in.

chunks.title: How does ALERT fund its community initiatives and ensure transparency?
chunks.text: ALERT is funded through individual philanthropic contributions, institutional donor grants, and corporate CSR partnerships. Our accounts are audited annually by statutory chartered accountants, filed with the Registrar of Societies, and submitted under FCRA guidelines to ensure absolute financial integrity.

chunks.id: news:Godavari Flood Relief 2023: Emergency Rations & Medical Kits to 4,200 Displaced Families
chunks.title: Godavari Flood Relief 2023: Emergency Rations & Medical Kits to 4,200 Displaced Families
chunks.text: ALERT mobilized field teams across flood-hit habitations of Alluri Sitharama Raju and Eluru districts, deploying mechanized boats to supply rice, lentils, drinking water, and sanitary kits to cut-off Adivasi hamlets. Reported September 2023.

chunks.title: Flood Relief Operations 2022: Multi-Mandal Relief Mission Across Submergence Habitations
chunks.text: Field caseworkers distributed comprehensive ration packets and hygiene supplies to families displaced by heavy Godavari river spillage in Kunavaram, VR Puram, and Chintoor mandals. Reported October 2022.

chunks.title: Flood Relief Operations 2021: Rescue Boat Deployment & Essential Services in Hill Tracts
chunks.text: ALERT established temporary relief distribution bases in remote hill areas, providing direct sustenance to vulnerable tribal children, nursing mothers, and elderly persons. Reported August 2021.

chunks.title: Blankets & Winter Care Distribution in East Godavari Hill Hamlets
chunks.text: Over 3,000 thermal wool blankets and basic healthcare supplies were handed over directly to remote Konda Reddi tribal households facing harsh winter temperatures. Reported October 2020.

chunks.text: Acres Forest Rights Secured: 15000+; Adivasi Families Supported: 25000+; Submergence Villages Monitored: 371; Off-Grid Solar Hamlets Energized: 75+; Yenadi Women in Cooperatives: 3500+; Families Emergency Relieved: 4200+. These are the figures published on the site.

chunks.title: About ALERT
chunks.text: ALERT — Association for Land Ecosystem Rights & Tribal Heritage. Founded 2004. Registered Society, Registration No. 307/2004 under the Societies Registration Act. Section 12A and Section 80G registered (80G receipts issued for donations). FCRA registered for receiving foreign contributions. Rights-based development for Adivasi and marginalized coastal communities: land and forest rights, rehabilitation entitlements, self-governance, livelihoods and child rights.

chunks.title: ALERT office, phone and email
chunks.text: Head office: Door No. 40-9/1-16, Sai Nagar, Near Benz Circle, Vijayawada - 520010, Andhra Pradesh, India. Phone +91 866 2482345. Mobile / WhatsApp +91 94401 82940. Email contact@alertngo.in or director@alertngo.in (also alertap.in@gmail.com). Founder Director: Y. L. J. B. Jayaraj (Founder Director). Website https://alertngo.in.

chunks.title: The four wings of ALERT's work
chunks.text: Forest Rights & Land: RoFR 2006 (IFR/CFR) claims, PESA self-governance, Andhra Pradesh Land Transfer Regulation Act 1 of 1970 restitution of alienated tribal land. Polavaram Rehabilitation: Land Acquisition & R&R entitlements for Project Affected Families of the Polavaram Irrigation Project under the RFCTLARR Act 2013. Livelihoods & Women: Antyodaya Matsya Mithra fisherwomen federation, micro-savings, indigenous millets and seed banks. Child Rights & Education: Bilingual education, nutrition, protection and statutory entitlements for Adivasi children.

chunks.title: Where ALERT works
chunks.text: Fifth Schedule / tribal tracts of Andhra Pradesh — Alluri Sitharama Raju and Parvathipuram Manyam districts, Rampachodavaram and Chinturu ITDAs, K.R. Puram ITDA belt, and the Krishna coastal belt.
